title: Punjab National Bank eyes debut dollar bond issue, bankers say - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
In September, PNB filed a $1.5 billion medium-term note programme, a precursor to the fundraising exercise. | Photo Credit: Karma Bhutia

One of India’s largest state-run lenders, Punjab National Bank, is set ​to tap the US dollar-denominated debt market through a ‌debut issue in the coming weeks under the ​central bank’s discounted swap window, two merchant ⁠bankers said on Friday.

Punjab National Bank is eyeing at least $500 million through a 5-year bond issue, and if ‌rates are favourable and demand is strong, it could raise up to $1 billion, the ‌bankers added.

The bankers requested anonymity as the ‌matter ⁠is still private, while the lender did ⁠not respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours.

“PNB was supposed to tap the market in late September ​or early October, but ‌may have delayed the exercise due to a sudden spike in Treasury yields,” one of the bankers said.

The bonds would be sold under the ‌discounted swap window, after the Reserve Bank ​of India allowed banks and state-run companies to raise funds overseas and access a ⁠subsidised hedging facility lowering the cost of managing currency risk since June.

The window is available until the end ‌of December, and another state-run lender, Canara Bank, is also looking to tap the dollar debt market.

In September, PNB filed a $1.5 billion medium-term note programme, a precursor to the fundraising exercise.

Moody’s and Fitch Ratings have assigned Baa3 and BBB- ratings to ‌the lender’s notes, in line with the issuer’s rating.

Indian lenders ​have already raised $13 billion through dollar bonds since the central bank announced the discounted scheme, ⁠with five state-run banks raising an aggregate of $3.5 billion through ⁠a combination of private placement and public issues.

State Bank of India, Bank of Baroda, ‌Union Bank of India, and Bank of Maharashtra are among the state-run peers that have used ​this route to raise cheaper funding.
